title: NDA's Election Streak Puts It in Pole Position for 2027
excerpt: After sweeping Bihar, Delhi, West Bengal, and Assam, the BJP-led alliance now commands an electoral college advantage that makes a third consecutive presidential win look inevitable.
body:
India's ruling National Democratic Alliance has strung together a remarkable run of state victories, and the prize now within reach is not just political momentum — it is the country's presidency itself.

**What happened — a sweep across India's map:**
The BJP won 48 of 70 seats in Delhi's assembly in February 2025, ending a decade-long AAP tenure and returning to power in the capital after 27 years. By November, the NDA secured a landslide victory in Bihar, winning 202 out of 243 seats in the state assembly. Then in May 2026, for the first time in history, the BJP captured power in West Bengal, winning 207 of the 293 seats declared. The BJP also won 82 of 126 seats in Assam, with NDA allies adding further seats to take the alliance well past the majority mark.

**Why it matters — the presidential arithmetic:**
Members of Parliament and Members of Legislative Assemblies — including elected representatives from Delhi and Puducherry — form the electoral college that elects India's President. The 2027 elections in India are expected to include the election of the President of India alongside Rajya Sabha and seven state assemblies. Each state win directly adds weighted votes to the NDA's tally in that college, and since the 2024 general election, the NDA has formed the government in 7 of the 11 states and union territories that have held assembly elections, including a return to power in Delhi and forming government in West Bengal for the first time.

**What to watch — 2027 and beyond:**
The 2027 elections will arrive on BJP terrain, against a party with state machinery, organisational depth, and now an eastern anchor it did not possess two years ago. Whether the opposition can consolidate around a single credible presidential candidate — or a convincing electoral college bloc — will define the contest.
